rationale: With the boundary question closed, I spent the remaining budget on a source-only check of the one question a reviewer is most likely to ask next: whether the module's own expectations make the classification deliberate rather than an omission, and whether anything in the snapshot would notice the gap. Reading the test files answers both. TestIsLocalMsg enumerates every message type in the enum except one - all 23 types from MsgHup to MsgStorageApplyResp, the type numbered 22 - and the single type it omits is MsgForgetLeader, the last-numbered type at 23, so nothing in that table pins its classification either way and the table itself was never extended to the newest type. The two tests that drive the inbound path for every message type - TestRawNodeStep on RawNode.Step and TestNodeStep on the public node.Step - both compute their expectation by calling IsLocalMsg on the very type under test, so a type absent from the table produces no assertion at all; the gap is structurally invisible to them, and classifying the type as local would break neither test. That does not by itself prove intent, so I recorded it as a fact in the index rather than inflating the finding: it tells a reviewer that the protection is untested for this type, and it removes the possible objection that a recorded expectation already endorses the current classification. The two test files are added as sources to the parent account with one sentence of context, since the account's defect claim rests on reading the absent entry as an omission.

interpretations.joint_history: The receipt 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624 was produced by a separate producer experiment, c5f8737038924695853b59262422afa9-experiment, filed under this question's child @legal_term_inbound rather than by this interpretation's own experiment acc6241dce584bc0a6817149dbe19f98-experiment. It is compatible as evidence for this question because it runs the same harness file on the same fixture family: three real RawNodes built from identical snapshots at index=10/term=1 with voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum and PreVote, HeartbeatTick=1, one real election, the same hand-delivered RawNode.Step inbound path, and a follower holding the same live leader context at term 2. The only difference is the field under test - that experiment delivers the same message type with a legal term where this question's own experiment delivered it with no term field - so the receipt extends the same comparison family (acceptance with an empty step error and Lead going 1 -> 0, plus the pre-vote consequence) to a second message form instead of measuring a different system, and its controls (indices 59 and 60) are the same under-lease and heartbeat controls this account already relies on. It does not supply or replace this account's reproducibility evidence, which remains the repeat 3f8d0a1b83304e5c9032b909703bb1c4 of this interpretation's own experiment.
interpretations.rationale: Current account across eight receipts, one of which is a repeat that reproduced the same experiment identically. A MsgForgetLeader in peer wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) is accepted with no error through both documented inbound paths - RawNode.Step (index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7, reproduced at 22 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a) and the real Node interface that applications use, where the node's own reported leader went 1 -> 0 and the same transition was produced by the intended local API Node.ForgetLeader (indices 42 and 43 of CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40, with the local-type control holding at 41). It changes the support a follower gives a log-up-to-date candidate: the identical pre-vote that produced no response under the lease is granted after the accepted message, the follower then grants the real vote, and the candidate becomes StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent still reports StateLeader at term 2 (indices 14, 15 and 17 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; index 25 of the latest). The window per message is closed by the next genuine leader message (heartbeat restored lead=1 after one leader tick, index 7, and the same pre-vote was ignored again, index 8), but a sender repeating the message each round keeps it open without any repair failing: three consecutive rounds restored the context and granted again (indices 32, 35, 38 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849, whose repair comparisons hold at 33 and 36). The harm stays bounded: after the forged election the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append, becomes a follower at term 3 following it, and the anchor equals the committed prefix it already had (index 26 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a), so no committed entry was lost. Cause and controls are unchanged, with one correction the newest receipt forces: MsgForgetLeader is absent from isLocalMsg although only the local ForgetLeader APIs produce it, and the term field is not what gates the message. Step's term switch matches only a zero, a higher and a lower term, so a non-zero term equal to the receiver's own falls straight through to the type switch and its default dispatch into stepFollower, where the type clears r.lead without reading the term; a receipt delivered exactly that well-formed form - From=3, a real voter, and Term=2, the follower's own term - and it returned no error, moved Lead 1 -> 0 and had the initially withheld pre-vote granted immediately afterwards (indices 61 and 62 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624, with the heartbeat and under-lease controls holding at 59 and 60). So the term-less form used by the earlier receipts was the weaker case rather than the load-bearing one, and the missing classification is sufficient on its own; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected or ignored in every receipt. Conditions the effect depends on, stated explicitly: the defeated lease test exists only when Config.CheckQuorum is set (inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout), so the marginal effect of the forged message is specific to CheckQuorum deployments; the type is a no-op on leaders, so the incumbent keeps serving until it learns a higher term; and a candidate whose log is behind is still refused by isUpToDate, so the message does not manufacture support for stale candidates. The exposure this creates is now measured rather than only bounded by reading: an elected leader that afterwards hears from nobody is already a follower at its first CheckQuorum check, with its term unchanged, and stays a follower at the next sample (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512), so the overlap between the incumbent and the forged leader lasts one election timeout of the incumbent's own clock in the silent case. Remaining limits are scope: single process, hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refusing the message outright, and the persistence loop using an exact one-message-per-tick cadence. The repeat of this very experiment from its retained inputs in a clean copy returned the same twelve comparison outcomes with the same witness indices (under-lease controls holding at 3, 4, 7 and 10; the peer-form message accepted at 5 and 13; the same pre-vote granted afterwards at 6 and 14; the vote granted at 15; the candidate leading at term 3 at 17; the repair heartbeat and the ignored pre-vote after it at 7 and 8), which is what makes the account schedule-stable rather than the product of one favourable interleaving. The later boundary receipt is a single execution rather than a repeat, so it extends the account's scope by one well-formed message form without inheriting that reproduction evidence. One review question this raises is whether the snapshot's own expectations contradict the reading, and they do not: the filter's expectation table in util_test.go enumerates every message type in the enum except one, running from MsgHup to MsgStorageApplyResp (the type numbered 22), and the only type it omits is MsgForgetLeader, the last-numbered type (23), while the two tests that drive the inbound path for every type - TestRawNodeStep on RawNode.Step and TestNodeStep on node.Step - derive their assertion from IsLocalMsg itself, so a type absent from the table cannot be caught by them; the omission is therefore invisible to the snapshot's own tests, which fits an oversight rather than a deliberate classification, and it also means that classifying the type as local would contradict no recorded expectation.
counterevidence: The competing explanation that followers grant pre-votes and votes regardless of their leader is excluded by the under-lease control in every receipt, including the control round inside the persistence loop, the Node-interface control, and the two controls of the boundary receipt (indices 59 and 60 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624).

The reading that the finding only fires because the delivered message left its term field unset - and so collapses into the separately refuted term-zero path - is now excluded by the well-formed delivery, which cleared the leader context with a legal term (index 61 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624).
The change is per-message and reversible: the context returns with the next real leader heartbeat in every round, so this is not a stuck state and does not survive a sender that stops.
The widest severity reading is excluded by the aftermath receipt: the deposed incumbent conceded and the new leader's log continued the committed prefix, so no committed entry was lost.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so lease-based reads are not broken by this mechanism.
limitations: Fault-model assumption: a peer may deliver a protobuf message of any type - including one the module only produces locally - to the documented inbound path, repeatedly; the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the protection under test, and the well-formed receipt shows the message needs no illegal field to be accepted.

Single-process, hand-delivered messages: no wall-clock duration, jitter, packet loss, authentication or multi-host transport behaviour is measured, and the persistence loop used an exact one-message-per-tick cadence.
The quorum-scale election uses one voter plus the candidate, and it was re-executed identically in the repeat, so its outcome is reproduced even though the quorum size itself was not varied.

The incumbent's overlap with the new leader is bounded and measured for the silent case - one election timeout of its own clock with an unchanged term (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512) - but that bound does not follow when the leader still hears from some voters, or when CheckQuorum is disabled.
The effect requires CheckQuorum to be enabled for the lease test it defeats, and it is a follower-side change only (leaders ignore the type).

Reproduction: the principal experiment was executed twice from its fixed inputs in clean copies and both runs produced identical comparison outcomes and witness indices; the boundary receipt that removes the dependence on the unset term was executed once, and messages carrying a higher term were not measured at all.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot's own tests do not pin IsLocalMsg(MsgForgetLeader) in either direction, and its inbound-path tests cannot detect a type missing from the filter. TestIsLocalMsg (util_test.go) enumerates every message type in the enum except one, listing all 23 types from MsgHup through MsgStorageApplyResp (the type numbered 22), and the single type every one of those entries omits is MsgForgetLeader, the last-numbered type (23). TestRawNodeStep steps a message of every type in MessageType_name through the real RawNode.Step and asserts ErrStepLocalMsg only when IsLocalMsg(msgt) is already true. TestNodeStep routes every type through the public node.Step and expects the receive channel to stay empty only when IsLocalMsg(msgt) is already true. Both tests read their expectation from the table under test, so neither would fail today for MsgForgetLeader, and neither would fail if the type were classified as local.
knowledge.conditions: Read from the captured snapshot as expectations, not executed in this run. RawNode.Step rejects a local-typed message with ErrStepLocalMsg when the sender is not a local thread id, whereas the public node.Step silently returns nil after ignoring it; the internal node.step path that node.ForgetLeader uses never passes through that check, which is why the two producers keep working either way.
